title: Smaller shares for general secret sharing
formal: Do there exist real constants K>0 and 0<c<1/2 such that, for every n≥1 and every monotone access structure Γ on [n] with ∅∉Γ and [n]∈Γ, there exists a perfect secret-sharing scheme for a uniform one-bit secret with max_i log₂|S_i|≤K·2^(cn), where S_i is the finite alphabet of participant i’s share?

definitions: [n]={1,…,n}. An access structure Γ⊆2^[n] is monotone when A∈Γ and A⊆B⊆[n] imply B∈Γ. A scheme is a joint probability distribution of a secret B uniform on {0,1} and shares X_i∈S_i, where each S_i is a finite nonempty set. For each A∈Γ there is a deterministic map r_A:∏_{i∈A}S_i→{0,1} such that r_A((X_i)_{i∈A})=B with probability one. For each A∉Γ, the conditional distributions of (X_i)_{i∈A} given B=0 and B=1 are identical. This is exact reconstruction and perfect information-theoretic privacy, with arbitrary collusion within A. Share size is the base-two logarithm of its alphabet cardinality, not its Shannon entropy or the sum over participants. It is normalized by the secret size of one bit. There is no linearity, field, threshold, computation-time or uniform construction requirement. The scheme may depend on the whole finite access structure. K,c must be universal. Rounding log₂|S_i| up to an integer encoding length changes K only by an absolute factor.

sentences: Secret sharing distributes a secret among participants so that authorized groups can reconstruct it and unauthorized groups learn nothing.
For unrestricted access structures, the amount of information stored in each share can grow exponentially with the number of participants.
The cited problem asks for a better general upper bound, specifically an exponential rate below one half in the stated normalization.
Improvements for special access structures do not resolve the worst-case requirement over all authorized-group patterns.
A stronger construction would reduce the storage cost of general perfect secret sharing and narrow a large gap between known upper and lower bounds.
